scope: Close the Java profession-level alias surface that can otherwise reconstruct NGE combat, entertainer, or trader levels without using getLevel or player_level.iff, while preserving the unrelated combat-simulator NPC profession UI.

findings: Publish 14.1 professions advance through skill boxes, XP pools, prerequisites, skill points, and training rather than a stored combat/entertainer/trader level tuple.
All respec profession-level alias calls are internal to the retired NGE profession-respec compatibility library, with no qualified external consumers.
The same-named combat simulator methods configure authored NPC actor professions in local script variables and do not read or mutate player respec state.

retiredRespecCompatibility.authority: The six compatibility methods and their internal calls are confined to respec.java; the sole workflow consumer is dominated by retireNgePlayerRespecEntrypoint and persisted state is removed during player lifecycle and CTS handling.

retainedNpcCombatSimulatorUi.authority: The standalone combat simulator's setProfessionLevel methods edit local simulated-actor configuration only and never invoke respec or mutate a player's profession-level array.
